title: Oldie but Goodie: Re-illuminating Label Propagation on Graphs with Partially Observed Features

problem.claim: Missing node features can make direct GNN use sub-optimal for downstream tasks such as node classification.

gap.claim: When only a few features are available, existing GNN-based methods may perform worse than traditional structure-based models.

contributions.claim: GOODIE combines Label Propagation and Feature Propagation branches to produce node embeddings under partial feature availability.
GOODIE uses a GNN-based decoder to align hidden embeddings from the Label Propagation branch with those from the Feature Propagation branch.
GOODIE uses Structure-Feature Attention and Pseudo-Label contrastive learning to combine structural and feature information and generate predictions for unlabeled nodes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GOODIE, its Structure-Feature Attention, and its Pseudo-Label contrastive learning as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GOODIE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods when few features are available and when features are abundant.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world graphs may have missing node features, which can make direct GNN use sub-optimal.
Existing GNN-based approaches may underperform traditional structure-based models when few features are available.
GOODIE combines Label Propagation and Feature Propagation, aligning their embeddings with a decoder.
Structure-Feature Attention and Pseudo-Label contrastive learning produce final predictions for unlabeled nodes.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance across sparse- and abundant-feature situations.

source_observation.claim: Structure-based propagation can remain useful when node features are sparse, while feature propagation can provide complementary information.

interpretation.claim: Hybrid models may be appropriate when the reliability of graph structure and node features varies across cases.

application.claim: For graphs with partially observed node features, consider combining structural and feature propagation with learned weighting.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which datasets, feature-missing mechanisms, or task conditions determine when the hybrid approach is preferable.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The feature-missing mechanism and proportions beyond the described sparse and abundant cases are not specified.
Ablation results and limitations are not specified.
